attach.why: Supplies each candidate's production rank among peers as one ballot feature for nfl.vote_outcome_model; it is not the winner rule, because the AP winner is the highest total of ranked-ballot points, not the maximum of production.

Ranked-ballot aggregator parametrised by voters, places and points vector per award and season (MVP top-5 10-5-3-2-1 and a top 5 for all eight AP awards in 2025 are seen in search-result copies only; earlier non-MVP schemes, the 2022 start and the tie rule are unverified) that turns candidate features into winner probabilities in stage s6.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials.target: A team's or both teams' additive count in a game (field goals, sacks, total yards, successful 2-point and 4th-down conversions) relative to a threshold.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials.mechanism: Per-game counts are opportunities times a per-opportunity rate: field goals follow drives that stall inside the kicker's range, sacks follow opposing dropbacks times a pressure-to-sack conversion, yards follow plays times yield per play, and two-point and fourth-down conversions follow each coach's decision to try times a success rate, all reshaped by score path, weather and overtime. Counts are overdispersed and discrete, so thresholds are tail masses of a mixture over score states; both-team counts add a script-driven negative dependence between teams. The multi-week next-interception series moved to its own archetype.

attach.why: Coach aggression on fourth downs and two-point tries and tempo drive field-goal attempts and the conversion counts.
Go-for-it versus kick policy and two-point policy by state set attempts for field goals and for the 2-point and 4th-down conversion counts.
Go-for-it policy on 4th-and-goal decides two-point attempts and goal-line fourth-down tries counted by KXNFL4DCONV and KXNFL2PTCONV.
Overtime probability adds possessions to counts if overtime counts and adds a small tail mass to dispersion; tie-count use sits in the league tie archetype.
Offensive success rate links to yards per play for the team-yards series and to short-yardage conversion; no first-down series is live.
Safety frequency is a rare-event tail input to the dispersion stage; generic and demoted to context.
Pressure drives sack counts for the team and game sack series.
Starting quarterback status and sack avoidance change dropbacks and sacks for team sacks and game sacks.
In-game quarterback exit risk changes the opposing sack pool and the team's yards; staged in the sack stage.
Practice and designation vintages feed the starting-quarterback availability probability used by the sack stage.
Plays per game bound every count; the opponent's pace and ball control matter as much as own pace.
Expected drives set the opportunities for field goals and stalled drives.
Kicker range and accuracy by distance, altitude and wind decide field-goal counts for KXNFLFG.
Sampled rules text fixes the counted object, thresholds, first-score and penalty clauses and what is left unstated (overtime, postponement, source), so settlement is read from it and not assumed.
In-game injury exit risk of the starting quarterback changes comeback and lead-change odds from the exit onward, a path event that pregame ratings cannot see.
Quarterback-specific hazard of leaving before the end of the game, by lead size, clock and mobility, used to switch the trailing or leading team to a backup in the simulated path.
Overtime points increment and probability by rule era: the only attached input that models whether and how overtime changes scores, needed for the regulation-only versus full-game readings.
Probability that a game ends level after overtime, which decides whether a game that was tied late can still produce a comeback win or a lead change.
Drive-result probabilities by start position over all drives, supplying mid- and late-game drive rates that the first-four-drives input does not cover.
Opponent-adjusted per-drive TD and FG rates by period, so the generator uses period-specific scoring for the 10-12 drives of a game and not only early-game rates.
Expected drives per team set the number of possessions in the simulated path and feed the market-free score-state input; without it the possession count is undefined.
Sampled rules text fixes the counted object, thresholds, first-score and penalty clauses and what is left unstated (overtime, postponement, source), so settlement is read from it and not assumed.
End-of-half hurry-up and clock management, the situation in which a quarterback spike on or inside the 1 can occur, which is a clock decision and not a pass call.
Quarterback-specific hazard of leaving the game by lead size, clock and mobility; the exit event that can put a non-quarterback in as the emergency passer.
Probabilities that a team's QB1 and QB2 slots are filled by named players, which tells who the emergency passer would be and whether a backup is listed at another position.
Opposing neutral pass rate over expected converts opposing plays into dropbacks, the volume factor of each game's hazard.
State-conditional total plays per game gives opposing plays for each window game, with lead effects.
The named team's defensive injuries and coverage scheme (cornerbacks and safeties with ball skills) shift its interception multiplier over a long window.
Man/zone and single-high/two-high shell rates of the named team's defence, a scheme determinant of takeaway rate.
